newsitem.title: USA: GE sets split, higher div, greater buyback. [corrected 16:18 gmt]
newsitem.headline: GE sets split, higher div, greater buyback. [corrected 16:18 gmt]

text.p: General Electric Co said its board voted Thursday to boost the quarterly dividend, increase the share repurchase program, and split the common stock two-for-one.
The moves by GE were widely anticipated by the market.
(Corrects from "GE confirmed to Reuters earlier in the week that it would announce the moves".)
The quarterly dividend was raised to $0.52 a share from $0.46, payable January 27, record December 31, the company said.
The board expanded the stock buyback program to $13 billion from $9 billion and extended the program through 1998, GE said.
Under the program, initiated in December 1994, GE has bought back $6.3 billion of stock -- or about 92 million shares -- in the past two years.

The increase in the program will enable GE to buy back shares at an annual rate of $3-$3.5 billion through 1998, GE said. The company said it expected the buyback program to boost its earnings per share growth rate and return on equity. It did not say by how much.
GE shareholders will vote on the expanded buyback program at the annual meeting on April 23, 1997, GE said.
Also at that time, shareholders will vote on the two-for-one stock split.
The company has about 1.64 billion shares outstanding. The split, if approved, would be GE's second in the past three years, the company said.
